newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks close up, properties lead rally.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks close up, properties lead rally.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks closed up on Friday, buoyed by the outlook for the local property market and positive trends on Wall Street, brokers said.
"Hongkong Bank's comments on the property market were reassuring and helped (market) sentiment," said James Osborn in institutional sales at ING Barings.

The Hang Seng Index closed 62.53 points higher at 13,404.14, after moving to a day high of 13,451.16 in the early trade. Turnover was HK$5.65 billion, slightly higher than Tuesday's HK$4.75 billion but well off Monday's HK$9.14 billion.
HSBC Holdings general manager Christopher Landgey said on Friday Hongkong Bank did not see any sign of a speculative bubble in the medium priced residential property market.
Osborn said developers' action to curb speculation in the luxury sector of the real estate market would also the sentiment.
The property sector outperformed the rest of the market. Red chips and second liners were also in demand, spreading trading activity broadly throughout the market, brokers said.
Cheung Kong led the property sector, gaining HK$1.00 to HK$69.50 on moderate turnover of HK$174.76 million.

Cheung Kong has risen on the view that the company will achieve an average sales price in excess of HK$7,000 per sq ft for its new, well located Laguna Verde development in Kowloon, said a property analyst at Merrill Lynch.
Osborn said the share was also boosted by the government's approval of the extension of Cheung Kong's Kingswood Villa development.
Sun Hung Kai Properties and New World Development both added HK$0.75 to HK$95.75 and HK$51.75.
Brokers said red chips were sought and would be a major theme of the market in the coming months.
CITIC Pacific was the best performing issue. The share rose to an all-time high of HK$43.90 then eased to close HK$1.40 higher at a new record close of HK$43.60.
China Resources leaped HK$1.00 to HK$15.50, a new all time record, then eased to a record close of HK$15.35.
Guangzhou Investment, one of the day's most actively traded issues, gained HK$0.20 to new record close of HK$3.45 on turnover of HK$133.64 million. The share set a new intra-day high of HK$3.475.
H share Luoyang Glass rose HK$0.15 to HK$2.425.
